**Bottom‑line recommendation:** Proceed **only if** the transaction is restructured and documented so that it meets the *public‑interest* and *community‑benefit* standards now required by both Pennsylvania (PA) and New Jersey (NJ) Attorneys‑General (AGs). The board should adopt a “conditional go‑ahead” that ties every key post‑transaction variable—charity care, staffing, payer mix—to enforceable commitments and independent verification. If those conditions cannot be met, the board should reject or postpone the deal. --- ## 1. Why the current materials are insufficient | Issue | What the AGs will look for (PA & NJ) | Risk if omitted | |-------|--------------------------------------|-----------------| | **Charity‑care obligations** | PAAG requires a *community benefit* analysis that quantifies free/discounted care; NJAG demands a similar “public interest” assessment. | Loss of tax‑exempt status, AG investigation, public backlash. | | **Staffing levels** | Both states scrutinize whether the nonprofit can maintain or grow its workforce post‑transaction (PA: § 1202.1(a)(3); NJ: § 18:5-4). | Unmet obligations → lawsuits from employees and unions; reputational damage. | | **Payer‑mix shift** | AGs evaluate whether the deal will disproportionately increase high‑cost uninsured or Medicaid patients, eroding community benefit (PAAG “public interest” test; NJAG “community impact” review). | Reduced revenue streams, higher uncompensated care burden. | The absence of these models means the board cannot demonstrate that the transaction preserves the hospital’s mission and public‑interest obligations—exactly what the AGs will demand. --- ## 2. Conditions for a conditional go‑ahead | Condition | What to do | Why it matters | |-----------|------------|----------------| | **Independent financial modeling** | Hire an external CPA/financial advisor to build detailed projections that include:
• Charity care volume & cost
• Staffing headcount & salary budgets
• Payer‑mix scenarios (baseline, 5 % shift, worst case) | Provides objective evidence for AG review and board approval. | | **Community benefit commitment** | Draft a *Community Benefit Plan* that:
• Sets minimum charity‑care dollars per year
• Guarantees staffing levels or provides a hiring plan
• Includes a payer‑mix target (e.g., no more than X% uninsured) | Meets PAAG §1202.1(a)(3) and NJAG public‑interest criteria; protects tax status. | | **Legal structuring** | Ensure the equity investment is structured as a *non‑profit‑friendly* partnership or limited liability company that:
• Keeps 501(c)(3) status intact
• Provides for a “non‑distributive” return to the nonprofit (e.g., preferred equity with capped dividends) | Avoids “tax avoidance” flags and AG scrutiny. | | **Conflict‑of‑interest & board approval** | Require full disclosure of any board member’s relationship with the PE sponsor; obtain a 2/3 vote after independent counsel review. | Satisfies PAAG’s fiduciary duty requirements and NJAG’s conflict rules. | | **Independent audit of post‑transaction metrics** | Agree that an external auditor will annually verify charity care, staffing, and payer mix against the plan. | Gives AGs a reliable source for enforcement; protects the nonprofit from future liability. | | **Contingency clause** | If any metric falls below threshold, the PE sponsor must:
• Provide additional capital
• Re‑invest in community benefit
• Or allow the nonprofit to terminate the deal with minimal penalty | Protects the hospital’s mission and financial health. | --- ## 3. Pennsylvania AG review (PAAG) | PAAG Requirement | How to satisfy it | |------------------|-------------------| | **Public‑interest test** – The transaction must be “beneficial” to the nonprofit’s mission and community. | Provide a detailed *Community Benefit Analysis* that quantifies free/discounted care, staffing retention, and payer‑mix impact. | | **Section 1202.1(a)(3)** – Hospitals must demonstrate ongoing community benefit. | Include charity‑care commitments in the Community Benefit Plan; attach independent projections to board minutes. | | **Tax‑exempt status** – PE deals can trigger “unrelated business income” if not structured properly. | Use a *non‑distributive* equity structure (e.g., preferred equity with capped dividends) and include a clause that any excess earnings are reinvested into community benefit. | **Key PAAG documents to submit:** - Community Benefit Plan (signed by PE sponsor). - Independent financial model. - Conflict‑of‑interest disclosure. --- ## 4. New Jersey AG review (NJAG) | NJAG Requirement | How to satisfy it | |------------------|-------------------| | **Public‑interest determination** – The deal must not erode the hospital’s charitable mission. | Provide a *public‑interest memorandum* that links the PE investment to measurable community outcomes (charity care, staffing, payer mix). | | **Section 18:5-4** – Hospitals must maintain “reasonable” levels of uncompensated care and workforce. | Include explicit staffing commitments in the Community Benefit Plan; attach projections showing no net loss of jobs or services. | | **Community benefit analysis** – Must show that the PE sponsor will not shift resources away from community service. | Attach a *payer‑mix impact study* with scenarios for worst‑case shifts and mitigation strategies (e.g., targeted Medicaid expansion). | **Key NJAG documents to submit:** - Public‑interest memorandum. - Community Benefit Plan. - Independent audit schedule. --- ## 5. Practical next steps 1. **Engage a nonprofit law firm** with PA & NJ AG experience within the next 30 days. 2. **Commission an independent financial model** (within 45 days). 3. **Draft the Community Benefit Plan** and have it signed by the PE sponsor before any board vote. 4. **Submit preliminary documentation** to both AGs for a “pre‑review” comment period (recommended within 60 days of board approval). 5. **Hold a special board meeting** with full disclosure, conflict checks, and a 2/3 vote on the conditional go‑ahead. 6. **Implement an annual audit** of charity care, staffing, and payer mix; report findings to the AGs and the board. --- ## 6. Bottom line - **Proceed only if** you can provide documented, enforceable commitments that satisfy PAAG’s public‑interest test and NJAG’s community‑benefit analysis. - **Do not proceed** if the transaction lacks independent modeling or fails to lock in staffing/charity care levels—those gaps expose the nonprofit to AG investigations, loss of tax exemption, and reputational harm. By meeting these conditions, the board can move forward with confidence that the private‑equity recapitalization will strengthen the hospital’s financial position **without compromising its charitable mission**.
